Nostramo, on the inside edge of the Ghoul Stars, is a planet of perpetual darkness, covered in clouds of pollution and a perpetual solar eclipse. Only the planetary elite could afford artificial illumination. Nostramo's geology contained priceless wealth, particularly huge quantities of naturally occurring adamantium. The planet's synchronicity with its moon, Tenebor, kept the planet under the darkness of a solar eclipse even in the height of summer. As a result, the human population of Nostramo had pale albino skin and black eyes adapted to live in an environment of near-total darkness. Konradia Curze became the city's first monarch. The few nobles who survived by swearing loyalty to her became her mouthpieces. She ruled with a fair and even hand, but any who transgressed would suffer. Konradia Curze eventually claimed the other four cities of Nostramo, bringing increased productivity and fearful peace to the world. Konradia left with the Emperor, the people felt they were free to speak their minds again, but replacing her autocracy with the Administratum soon became a return to the old ways. Eventually Ashkar Skraivok launched a coup that massacred the Imperial Governor and his cabinet. Ashkar did not secede from the Imperium, but declared the old ways of Nostramo were to be restored.

entries.name: Word Bearers
entries.content: The Word Bearers, originally known as the Imperial Heralds and the Iconoclasts, is the XVII Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions. Their colour scheme is Grey. The Word Bearers Legion were divided into many different Chapters, each bearing a name and icon representing one of the constellations of Colchis. Typically a Chapter consisted of several companies with an overall strength of 500-3,000 warriors. While each Chapter maintained a formal military structure consisting of a Chapter Master, Captains and so on there was also a parallel hierarchy based around Chaplains and spiritual authority. The legion fleet was known to be composed of an armada of a mere 116 warships. The Word Bearers are unique due to their extreme religious and worshiping the Emperor as a God publicly. The Word Bearers fight with utter devotion and a fanatical zeal. Upon defeating an enemy, the Word Bearers would empty their libraries and records of any contents deemed heretical or sorcerous. Condemned works, individuals, and buildings would be destroyed. In their place, vast monuments and cathedrals, all dedicated to the Emperor, were erected. The greatest Chaplains of the Legion produced enormous works on the divinity and righteousness of the Emperor. While other Legions were rapidly conquering planet after planet, the Word Bearers proceeded much more slowly, as they would build temples and shrines in veneration of the Emperor, who was also deemed the God, on each newly conquered planet.

entries.name: Colchis
entries.content: Colchis is the homeworld of the Word Bearers Space Marine Legion. Colchis is a massive world, three times larger than Terra. It took 4.8 Terran years to orbit its sun and 170.4 Terran hours to rotate once around its axis, giving it an extended day-night cycle; thus, the Colchisian civilizations developed a unique method for keeping track of time. With this extended solar day, time was broken up into seven sub-days, known as Dawnaway, Mornday, Long Noon, Post-noon, Duskeve, Coldfall, and High Night. These sub-days are further divided into three segments (wake-rise, wake-main, and rest-eve) to correlate more closely with a Terran day. The Mountains and deserts dominated the dry land of Colchis and civilisation clustered along coastlines, relying on water and air travel between settlements. Its capital city-state was Vharadesh, the City of Grey Flowers. Life on Colchis is often harsh outside of the cities which were all controlled by a religious institution known as the Covenant.

entries.name: Monarchia
entries.content: Monarchia, also known as the Perfect City of the Word Bearers, is the capital city of the planet Khur.

entries.name: Kor Phaeron
entries.content: Kor Phaeron is Lorgaria's foster father and spiritual advisor on Colchis, and the Primarch trusted her counsel most of all. Kor Phaeron followed the Primarch through all her battles against the Covenant, providing her spiritual guidance as the battles seemed to have no end. As Lorgar took command of her Legion, Kor Phaeron became her second-in-command, becoming the First Captain of the Word Bearers Legion. Kor Phaeron is power-hungry, zealous, manipulate, and aggressive man. But has fondness for Lorgaria. Kor Phaeron rejects Lorgaria's concept of One God, instead secretly believing in the Covenant's concept of Four Deities which secretly were the Chaos Gods.

entries.name: Erebus
entries.content: Erebus is one of the most prominent members of the Word Bearer. He is going to be  instrumental in converting first Lorgaria and then Horacia to Chaos. Erebus refers to himself as Destiny's Hand, the mortal instrument of the plans of the Ruinous Powers. Erebus was born to common parents on Colchis and even at a young age felt it was his purpose to manipulate, deceive, and sow discord. He felt a thrill testing his own limits in these acts, which in its earliest form manifested as him teasing desert scorpions. The Ruinous Powers had always been with him and guided his actions even as a young boy.

entries.name: Void shield
entries.content: Void shields are energy fields employed by the Imperium to protect everything from Super-Heavy Vehicles to massive starships. The shields operate via Warp technology, absorbing the energy of attacks and displacing them into the Immaterium. Void shields benefit from the fact that they can be raised again after taking damage and collapsing, even in the midst of combat. Void shields extend some distance from their point of origin, thus in some cases it is possible for an enemy to penetrate the shield and cause damage directly to the target. Activated void shields create a translucent bubble around their target, one which distorts visual light attempting to pass through and so creating an optical hazing effect. When displacing weapon impacts void shields ripple like gelatine and create a kaleidoscope of colours.

entries.name: Raven Guard
entries.content: The Raven Guard were the XIX Legion of the original Space Marine Legions. Their Primarch is Corvina Corax. Their homeworld is Lycaeus, a moon which orbits the Hive World Kiavahr. The Raven Guard specialise in guerrilla warfare, moving behind enemy lines with unrivaled stealth and striking with precise application of force. Their colour scheme is Black, white. Right pauldron trim colours show company. The Raven Guard are known for hitting weak points in enemy defenses hard and they perform lightning strikes upon locations of tactical importance to cripple their enemy. The Raven Guard disdain the notion of recklessly charging into enemy ranks. The Raven Guard rely heavily on their Scouts for pinpointing enemy positions and to scout for good drop sites. The Raven Guard also make extensive use of Assault Squads as well as any other formation that uses Jump Packs. The Tactical Squads of the Raven Guard are often deployed via Thunderhawks or Drop Pods. The favorite weapons of the Raven Guard Commanders are the Lightning Claws in addition to their Jump Packs. Raven Guard Captains are fiercely independent, and it's incredibly rare for the chapter to fight as a whole. Individual companies are completely autonomous. Core to Corax’s teachings was the Trifold Path of Shadow. The first path of shadow is Ambush, the second Stealth, and the third Vigilance. The Raven Guard makes less use of heavier vehicles and tanks. They conversely make heavy use of Land Speeders and Thunderhawk gunships. The Shadowmasters or Mor Deythan are a unit of Raven Guard. They are ordinary battle-brothers who had their primarch's ability to Shadow-walk. One unique trait about the Shadowmasters is that they were completely unknown to their own legion.

entries.name: Lycaeus
entries.content: Lycaeus, also known as Deliverance, is a moon orbiting the world of Kiavahr. It is the homeworld of the Raven Guard and the site of the Legion's fortress-monastery, the Ravenspire. Lycaeus is a mineral-rich moon orbiting the Forge World of Kiavahr. Originally the moon was populated by exiles from Kiavahr, slaves and criminals who lived in crude force domes that protected them the vacuum of space. These exiles were forced to work in the massive mineworks under the watchful eyes of overseers from the world below. These circumstances changed drastically with the coming of the Primarch Corax, who united the oppressed workers and led a revolution against the ruling Tech-Guilds. After the successful liberation of their homeworld the slaves renamed the moon Deliverance. Shortly after this, the Emperor arrived on Deliverance and the world was integrated into the Imperium and was made the homeworld of the XIX Legion.

entries.name: Ravenspire
entries.content: The Ravenspire is the fortress-monastery of the Raven Guard Legion on Deliverance. The tallest tower of the Ravenspire, is the roost of Corax herself.

entries.name: Salamanders
entries.content: The Salamanders are the XVIII Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions created by the Emperor of Mankind. Their Primarch is Vulkana. The Salamanders are known for their great hardiness as warriors and strong constitutions, willpower and devotion to humanity. Their scheme colour is Green, Black and Gold. Salamanders have dark or jet black skin and bright, burning eyes. A unique genetic trait the Salamanders have is Fire-Sight. This visual sensitivity to infrared emissions allows Salamanders to focus on particular heat signatures. They have greater tolerance of extreme temperature and radiation and a higher level of cellular repair. Drawing from the teachings of Vulkana, the Salamanders are renowned as compassionate towards the average people and as defenders of the weak. The Salamanders live amongst the civilians of their homeworld Nocturne and serve as guardians, exemplars, and caretakers. The Salamanders always evinced a readiness to ally themselves with other Imperial forces. The Salamanders follow the doctrines of their Promethean Cult, which places high emphasis on self-reliance, self-sacrifice, loyalty and collective decision-making. Flamers, Melta Weapons and Thunder Hammers are widely used throughout the Legion. They have strong affinity for close-range combat. All Salamanders are fully capable of maintaining and performing moderate repair on their weapons and armour, leaving the Legion's artificers with the free time necessary to create great works of technology and metallurgy. Which is why they have high number of Master-Crafted Weapons, Artificer Armour and Tactical Dreadnought Armour. Trained never to give up or retreat, Salamanders are capable of going on when their entire squad is dead.

entries.name: Nocturne
entries.content: Nocturne is the homeworld of the Salamanders Space Marine Legion. It is a binary planetary system, with its over-sized moon Prometheus circling Nocturne erratically causing massive tectonic stress. There are vast chains of volcanoes and frequent earthquakes, destroying what little the people built. The enormous levels of stellar radiation present on the world has given most of its life a dark obsidian-like appearance, including its people. Once every fifteen Terran years (One Nocturne year), the two worlds approach so closely that Nocturne is almost torn to pieces. This is the Time of Trial. Vast waves crash across the seas, thousands of volcanoes explode, and earthquakes constantly ravage the land. Then, a terrible winter sets in for the next quarter of a year. During this Time of Trial, the Sanctuary Cities throw open their gates and give refuge to the vast pilgrimages of the tribes who flee. Although the majority of Nocturne's populace are tribal in nature, there are 7 major population centres that exist on the surface of Nocturne. These are called the 'Sanctuary Cities'. Each of the cities contains a Legion Bastion of the Salamanders. The location of these Sanctuary Cities are situated upon the most seismically stable areas of Nocturne. The Seven great Sanctuary Cities are Themis, Epimethus, Heliosa, Aethonian, Clymene, Hesiod, and Skarokk.

entries.name: Prometheus
entries.content: Prometheus is Nocturne's moon and the Fortress-monastery of the Salamanders. The monastery is the only construction built there and is the centre of the Salamanders logistics and administration. Being an over-sized moon, it causes massive stress on Nocturne's tectonic plates, resulting in an event, known as the Time of Trials, which occurs every Nocturne year. Prometheus is also home to the Hall of Relics, a vast area containing a great number of shrines and reliquaries devoted to heroes of the Legion. Within its walls, shrines can be found to the great Firedrake Vulkan slew during his trials against the Outlander. Prometheus is the site of the Salamanders Fleet and as such, it plays host to a great dock where the Legion's ships can be restored.

entries.name: Promethium
entries.content: Promethium is a general term for any form of fuel in the Imperium. The term also commonly refers to the substance used as fuel for Imperial flamer weapons, a highly volatile incendiary gel which immediately ignites on contact with oxygen. It reaches super hot temperatures. Similar to napalm, the gel sticks to an individual, continuing to burn on its own accord, even underwater and in space. It also fuels most spacecraft and vehicles, both military and civilian.

entries.name: War Hounds
entries.content: The World Eaters, formally known as the War Hounds, are the XII Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions. Angron renamed the World Eaters in honour of her gladiator force she had led in rebellion on Nuceria. Their Primarch is Angron, sometimes known as the Red Angel. Their colour scheme is white and blue. The World Eaters favour close assaults, and this doctrine only grew more pronounced under the command of Angron. They are peerless in martial savagery, thanks in part to the effects of the psycho-surgical implants known as the Butcher's Nails that most had. Angron did little to change the higher-level organisation of the legion, with the echelons only undergoing a slight biasing towards line infantry once she took command. The World Eaters as a legion force are hybrid of tactical and close assault units, also possessing significant amounts of support elements useful to close assaults, such as Terminators and Land Speeders. World Eaters are champions of the drop-pod assault, usually choosing to drop in the heart of the enemy's defences. While infantry assault was their primary stratagem, the legion has armour and artillery units, and are highly adept in their use. The warfare carried out by the World Eaters was highly attritional not just in manpower, but materiel also. The most elite formation in the legion are the Devourers, the twelve-strong bodyguard group to Angron herself.

entries.name: Butcher's Nails
entries.content: The Butcher's Nails were a form of psycho-surgery conducted on the world of Nuceria, the adopted homeworld of Angron. Bearing resemblance to a lobotomy, large amounts of nails trailed with cables which resemble dreadlocks were inserted through the skull and into the brain to amplify the anger and rage of the subject. The surgery was reserved for the slave-gladiators of Nuceria. Angron was subject to the surgery. The Butcher's Nails are surprisingly complex and sophisticated. None of the Emperor's best Tech-Priests could remove the devices without killing Angron in the process.

entries.name: Bodt
entries.content: Bodt was a world of the Imperium close to the galactic core that served as the primary training and mustering ground for the World Eaters Legion. Acting as the Legion's de facto homeworld, its terrain was arid and volcanic. Bodt is a "barracks" world and proving grounds for the World Eaters. As the World Eaters conducted live fire exercises and established industry upon Bodt, it became a polluted, unstable, and toxic planet. Bodt also maintained a vault of ancient and forbidden weapons overseen by Tech-Priests from Sarum, known as the Crimson Priests.

entries.name: Nuceria
entries.content: Nuceria is the original homeworld of the Primarch Angron after she and the other Primarchs were scattered across the Warp. Nuceria was a brutal, unforgiving world run by cruel slavemasters from the city of Desh'ea that forced their subjects to battle in gladiatorial arenas. The aggression-enhancing technology known as the Butchers Nails was a key part of this process. The young Angron was captured and forced to take part in this cruel game until she led a slave revolt. However, at the height of the battle against the slavemasters, she was teleported away by the Emperor, something that infuriated her. In the aftermath of Angron's unwilling departure from Nuceria, her comrades were defeated and massacred by the slavemasters.

entries.name: Iron Hands
entries.content: The Iron Hands are the X Legion of the twenty original Space Marine Legions. Their Primarch is Ferrea Manus. The Iron Hands are notable for their heavy use of bionics and their reverence for all things mechanical, and thus their close ties to the Adeptus Mechanicus. Their colour scheme is Black and Silver. The Iron Hands are relatively straightforward and incredibly harsh. They are on poor terms with the Raven Guard. The Iron Hands are infamous for their extensive use of bionics. Between battles or on their warships while in the Warp, Iron Hands often spend time uploaded to cryo-pods, inloading tactical schematics and information. This aids the over-arching strategic hexamathic formulae that they deploy while on campaign known as the Calculus of Battle. This system seeks to break down wars to raw data and numbers, where enemy actions, logistics, casualties, and environmental elements can be predicted and balanced like an equation. Once a conclusion has been reached, the Iron Hands' nihilistic brutality translates well to war. When they attack, they do so without hesitation or mercy and will show little regard to the well-being of allies. This ruthlessness extends even their own Battle-Brothers, who will be coldly sacrificed to achieve an objective should it be necessary. This does not deter warriors of the Iron Hands however. Iron Hands fear no death and view injury in battle as something that should be sought. The Iron Hands rarely commit to a campaign unless overwhelming victory is all but guaranteed.

entries.name: Medusa IV
entries.content: Medusa IV, commonly referred to as Medusa, is the Homeworld of the Iron Hands Space Marine Legion. Medusa is a Waste World, that is a harsh realm of perpetual gloom, located extremely close to the Eye of Terror. With a dark and polluted sky, Medusa's sun rarely shines on the planet's surface and the world's geology is highly unstable, with earthquakes and volcanic eruptions constantly creating and destroying mountain ranges and seas. The people of Medusa are hardy and flourish despite the hostile environment. The population is broken up into clans who viciously compete and vie for natural resources and safe ground, save a few areas of relative calm which are mostly reserved for the Iron Hands Legion. As the nomadic clans seek a new settlement, great caterpillar-like mining haulers carry their personal possessions and resources. It is because of its harsh environment that Medusa is considered to be a Death World, in all but name.

entries.name: Blood Angels
entries.content: The Blood Angels, originally known as the Revenant Legion, are the IX Legion of the Space Marine Legions under their Primarch Sanguinia. They are well known for their bloodthirsty nature in battle. They are also one of the most long-lived Legion, and have a refined aesthetic sense. Their colour scheme is Blood Red Armour with Black Aquila, and their Helmet colour denotes squad type. The sons of Sanguinia have handsome and noble features, mimicking that of their Primarch. They have retractable fangs that are dubbed the Angel's Teeth. Blood Angels are noble warriors that were also well-versed in art and poetry. They strive for perfection be it in their works or art, martial discipline, or military doctrine. The Blood Angels will spare no effort to attain the material needed to create the Legion's art and have even fought wars to obtain them.

entries.name: Baal
entries.content: Baal is the homeworld of the Blood Angels and the base of the Legion's fortress-monastery, Arx Angelicum. Baal's two moons are called Baal Primus and Baal Secundus, from which the Blood Angels take their new recruits from all three worlds. The Blood Angels Primarch, Sanguinia, fell upon Baal Secundus after she and her brother Primarchs were scattered across the galaxy by the machinations of the Gods of Chaos. In ancient days Baal and its moons had earth-like atmospheres. Baal itself was always a world of red rust deserts, but its moons were close to paradises. As the Dark Age of Technology ended in the Age of Strife, civil war erupted between the world and its colonised moons, leading to the nuclear devastation of the planets.

entries.name: Arx Angelicum
entries.content:
Arx Angelicum is the Fortress-Monastery of the Blood Angels Space Marine Legion. It is located on the Blood Angels' homeworld of Baal. The Arx is built in and around an ancient, extinct volcano with two peaks which lies in the Endless Desert. The caldera of the largest peak was remade into a great wall known as the Arx Murus, which circles the Dome of Angels. Arx Murus is the outer wall which circles the Dome of Angels. Many of the Legion key buildings are built upon this outer layer. Needle-thin is the tower upon the Arx Murus that holds the chambers of the Sanguinia.Heavenward Redoubt is the fortress's keep.
Walk of Angels is Open statue-lined path leading to the Dome of Angels. Dome of Angels is an Retractable armour-glass that covers the whole interior of the Fortress. Verdis Elysia is a farming area where the Blood Angels grow their food. Sanguis Corpusculum is the Apothecarion.

entries.name: Thousand Sons
entries.content: The Thousand Sons are the XV Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions. Their Primarch is Magna, oft called Magna the Red. Their colours scheme is resplendent crimson with, bronze, and ivory trims and shoulder pads. Magna placed great emphasis on ensuring that legion officers could operate independently from her, going to lengths to ensure they were taught all that she believed they would need to succeed at command, including otherworldly skills. The individual Thousand Sons squads were led by those who showed the most psychic potential. These junior officers were also effectively apprenticed to more experienced officers for cult training. Veterans of the Thousand Sons wore the Achean-Pattern Power Armour with distinctive helmets and shoulder pads. The Thousand Sons rarely ever took to the field in great numbers. They would normally operate in small detachments, whose leader hold much more independent authority than officers. The Thousand Sons operated several Fellowships roughly equivalent to Companies. Each Fellowship was led by a powerful Psyker. Spread out among these Fellowships were several Cults that specialised in different Psychic disciplines. For the Thousand Sons, Magna is their literal saviour. Magna instituted her Cult system within her legion, five teachings that would allow her warrior-scholars to expand their knowledge, principally from her, at her position as master of all the cults; the rank of Magus. From this position atop a pyramidal teaching structure, Magna was able to direct and control her legion's psychic and philosophical development, all Thousand Sons looked to her for example and guidance. High percentage of Thousand Sons manifesting some level of psychic ability. Unfortunately this also brought with it a curse; a debilitating flaw of the Flesh Change, a degeneration into mindless, mutated, monstrosities. Which is linked with sustained, heavy, use of psychic powers. For the Thousand Sons, knowledge is power, and the most knowledgeable, the most powerful. They are more loyal to Magna than the Emperor. Sekhmet are Magna's elite Honour Guard.

entries.name: Prospero
entries.content: Prospero is the Homeworld of Magna the Red and her Space Marine Legion, the Thousand Sons. Prospero is a desolate but beautiful, dark planet and was chosen by its inhabitants because of its distance from Terra. Mutants and Psykers lived in reclusion and study, and Magna fit in well with this group due to her incredible psychic potential. It had one major city, Tizca, a gleaming city of white marble, with spires reaching into the sky. It was situated on the most central of the many mountains of the planet, nourished by underground hydroponics and techno-psychic collectible arrays providing sustainable energy. All the towers were gleaming and there were soaring obelisks and towering pyramids.

entries.name: Tizca
entries.content: Tizca is the capital city of the world Prospero. Described as one of the greatest cities of mankind, Tizca (also known as the City of Light) was a center for knowledge and beauty. Dominated by massive pyramid shaped structures, Tizca was designed in a radial pattern from the center to maximize order and asthetic beauty. All buildings, even industrial structures, were designed to be functional as well as pleasing to the eye. The pyramids of Tizca were reflective, designed to mirror the sky to enhance the beauty of the city's skyline. Located on the coast, Tizca also had a large port for ocean vessels. The part of the city closest to the coast was known as Old Tizca, an irregular layout of streets and buildings that existed before Magna designed the rest of the city in a more orderly pattern. Old Tizca was built on a gentle slope that led down to the sea and was where many of the city's diversions were found. Notable Locations are Pyramid of Photep and the Great Library of Tizca.

entries.name: Pyramid of Photep
entries.content: The Pyramid of Photep is the largest and most magnificent structure in Tizca, capital of Prospero. Built of gold and silver, the Pyramid was the personal sanctum of Magna the Red. It was also a site where Prosperan scholars and intellectuals could gather for discussion and debate.

entries.name: Great Library of Tizca
entries.content: The Great Library of Tizca is one of the grandest sites of Tizca, capital of Prospero. A massive leaf-topped pyramid of glass with a huge golden arch as its gateway, the Library was surrounded by a verdant park which many artisans and scholars of Prospero attended. The Library is the greatest repository of Human history and culture in the Galaxy as the Thousand Sons collected works from across the stars.

entries.name: Alpha Legion
entries.content: The Alpha Legion, also known as the Ghost Legion during the early Great Crusade, is the XX Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions. The Alpha Legion are renowned as the most secretive of all the Legions. The Alpha Legion's most closely guarded secret, unbeknownst to all but a few outside the legion, is that they had two primarchs; Alpharia and her twin Omegis, sometimes referred to collectively as just Alpharia Omegis. The Alpha Legion's veterans are experts in infiltration, covert operations, and manipulating events in their favor without revealing themselves or engaging in open warfare. Their armies also contain regular Humans known as Operatives. Their colour scheme is Silver, blue and green. Extensive preparations are made before actually attacking an target, including using spies. The Alpha Legion develops special weapons and technologies in secret without Imperial approval or knowledge. Alpha Legion forces operate secret arms factories and caches both inside and outside Imperial space. The Alpha Legion is the first Legion to produce Bolter shells specifically designed to penetrate Ceramite Power Armour. The Alpha Legion has chameleon technologies that allow them to outwardly change their appearances and mimic not only other legionnaires but also humans. Alpha Legion squads succeeded as a group or not at all, foolhardy heroics are frowned upon. The Legion's philosophy is that they are body of one that could strike in many places at once. Decisions within the Legion were made in a fairly open and reasonably democratic way, with all ranks allowed to interject and comment freely during planning sessions. The Alpha Legion internally discussed matters of philosophy and galactic policy. Alpha Legion equivalents of companies, battalions and chapters are known as "Harrows", "Cohorts", "Hosts" and "Instruments". The Alpha Legion saw itself as legion capable of operating even if the head were to be severed. Standard Space Marines assuming the mantle of their Primarch to confuse outsiders. When asked by non-Legion members, all Legionaries gave their names as "Alpharia", even when more than one was present.

entries.name: Space Wolves
entries.content: The Space Wolves, also Warriors of Russ, Vlka Fenryka or Wolves of Fenris, are the VI Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions. Their primarch is Lena Russ, and have the reputation as the Emperor's executioners and instruments of punishment. The Space Wolves are notorious throughout the rest of the Imperium for their ferocity in battle and their defiance of authority. Their colour scheme is Grey with yellow shoulder pads. Space Wolves have enhanced, animalistic abilities, including hyper-acute senses of hearing and smell, and a ferocity in battle that is almost unrivalled by any other astarte. The physical changes in the Wolves more extreme than those of other genetically-modified humans, such as elongated canines, shaggy hair that becomes grey, then pure white as the Wolf ages, and sometimes pale yellow eyes. Though undeniably loyal to the Emperor, the Space Wolves are fiercely anti-authoritarian. But they unquestionably carry out the Emperor's orders regardless of what it might be. The Space Wolves regard themselves as the Imperium's ultimate weapon, and are proud of it. The Space Wolves are also renowned for their passion for eating, drinking, and storytelling, when not engaged in battle. In contrast to the monastic habits of other Legions, they enjoy boisterous feasting, eating enormous amounts of meat and guzzling liquor so potent that it would eat through the guts of a normal human. But they are discipline, focused, dangerous and capable of anything. The Space Wolves apply great attention to planning, coordination in battle, the encirclement of the prey and the cleanliness of the kill.

entries.name: Fenris
entries.content: Fenris is the homeworld of the Space Wolves Space Marine Legion and their Fortress-Monastery, The Fang. It is located relatively close to the Eye of Terror. A planet of fire and ice, Fenris orbits its sun once every 3-4 Terran years. During the summer months volcanoes erupt, burning great areas with lava flows and churning the seas, spreading great floods and tidal waves. As the planet enters its long winter, the temperature drops so far that most of it actually ices over, giving the planet the appearance of a snowball from orbit. Numerous asteroid strikes, mutable coastlines and even swiftly risen or sunk island masses have resulted in the population becoming one of largely nomadic barbarian tribes. The tribes constantly seek secure territory, and as a result skirmishes and feuds over land between rival tribes are common. The central sea of Fenris is the Savage Sea or Worldsea, home to most of the planet's wildlife, most of which are vicious sea creatures. The Fang is located on the highest peak of a mountain range towards the centre of Asaheim. The Fang is the greatest fortress constructed since the fortifications of the Imperial Palace on Terra. It is so big as to pierce the atmosphere of Fenris, providing a docking point for orbiting spacecraft and allowing quick access to the surface. It is clad in immensely thick armour and is protected by void shields stronger than those on the Imperial warships. Shafts have been cut into the mountainside, concealing vast defense laser batteries capable of blasting the biggest ships in the galaxy. The top of The Fang is the centre of the Space Wolves' fleet dock where hundreds of ships are moored.

entries.name: Malcador the Sigillite
entries.content: Malcador the Sigillite is the First Lord of Terra. He is a powerful psyker who could communicate over long distances and wield immense power. He is a close adviser to the Emperor and the man credited with founding the Administratum of Terra. Malcador is over 6,000 years old and remembers his date of birth to the second. Malcador is a surviving member of an ancient order known as The Sigillites, which sought to gather and preserve the greatest and most powerful artifacts in Human history. Malcador's real name is Brahm al-Khadour, a Perpetual known as a cursed wanderer. Malcador is slender and unassuming figure dressed in pale robes, he has his staff of office and the force of his psychic presence. Malcador is very frail and sickly, and is an image he deliberately cultivated in order to have his enemies underestimate his formidable power. Malcador wears an archaeotech collar around his neck, which was capable of generating a powerful force field that would redirect an enemy's attack back at them. His staff was capable of unleashing a wave of nuclear fire, but is more a tool rather than a weapon. Malcador is the most powerful human psyker in the galaxy after the Emperor himself and potentially Magna the Red. He has physical resilience unnatural for a man of his apparent age and frailty.

entries.name: Remembrancer
entries.content: The Remembrancer Order is a group of poets, journalists, imagists and writers that are sent to accompany the Imperial forces during the later years of the Great Crusade, once the Emperor had returned to Terra. The Order of Remembrancers are ratified by the Council of Terra, directly to the Emperor with the goal of forming an order of people to be the Imperium's memory of its foundation and reflect the truth of the Great Crusade. Almost 4.3 million remembrancers were sent abroad, assigned to join all the key expedition fleets active in the expanding Imperium. They are generally disliked by both the regular troops and the Astartes.

entries.name: Phoenix Guard
entries.content: Phoenix Guard is the elite unit of Emperor's Children Space Marines who were responsible for performing various formal and ceremonial roles and served as the Primarch Fulgrim's bodyguards. Phoenix Guard followed their beloved Phoenician wherever she went as part of their duties. The Phoenix Guard consisted of both standard Power Armour and Terminator Space Marines. Acting as honor guards for not only Fulgrim but also as an elite cadre that guarded officers that had gained the Primarch's favor. The greatest of the Phoenix Guard are known as Phoenix Wardens and acted as the personal guards of Fulgrim herself. The Phoenix Guard wield Phoenix Power Spears, deadly arcane Power Halberds based on the Guardian Spears of the Custodies.

entries.name: Deathshroud
entries.content: The Deathshroud are Mortaria's personal bodyguard. Two accompany her at all times and are never more than forty-nine paces from her side. They are space marines who are listed as killed in action and then wear a mask for the rest of their lives so that only Mortaria may know their true identity. They carry their own Manreapers, copies of the Mortaria's own weapon proportionate for their hands.

entries.name: Olympia
entries.content: Olympia is the Homeworld to the Iron Warriors Space Marine Legion and Perturaya. Olympia is a rugged, mountainous world whose population was concentrated within many city states, spread across the planet's surface. The planet has vast amount of stone available and as such large fortresses were built. One of the city states, the home to the Primarch Perturaya, was named Lochos. A secular, opportunistic culture, given to the pursuit of wealth, security and dominance, the Olympian arts of war evolved towards a sublime mastery of fortress-building, siege craft and stone masonry. On Olympia, power was the ability to not only take resources but to defend them.

entries.name: Iron Warriors
entries.content: The Iron Warriors are the IV Legion of the twenty Space Marine Legions, sons of the Primarch Perturaya. Their specialty is siege warfare and the reduction of fortified positions as well as of building defensive fortifications and fortresses, which made them natural rivals of the Imperial Fists. Their methodical attitude made them merciless men in battle and siege, and fierce close-range fighters. They make common use of Imperial Army soldiers for cannon-fodder and to locate the positions of enemy gun emplacements. The Iron Warriors found itself constantly diminishing in active crusading size as units were detached to act as garrison troops watching over worlds in the process of compliance, order directly from the Emperor. The Iron Warriors did little to improve relations with the rest of the Imperium's armed forces. They maintained a cold and rude relationship with their fellow Space Marine Legions, while to the Imperial Army suffer high casualties from under Iron Warriors command. When at war and after the siege works were built there was a choice given to the besiegers; either to throw down their arms or the Iron Warriors would show no mercy. It maintained a special unit known as the Stor-Bezashk. The strategic command of the Legion is overseen by Grand Battalions, which functioned similarly to a Chapter, but had a larger stockpile of armor, artillery, and logistical support than other Legions. The Iron Warriors are organised as a number of Grand Companies each commanded by a Warsmith. The Iron Warriors' Warsmiths could match skills with Tech-priest. The Iron Warriors have a substantial war fleet of over 100 capital class ships. Iron Warriors colour scheme is Silver armour, gold trim, black shoulder pads.

entries.name: Stor-Bezashk
entries.content: The Stor-Bezashk is a prestigious unit of the Iron Warriors. The brotherhood was made up of the elite siege masters of the Legion and commanded mighty siege weapons unseen outside of the Adeptus Mechanicus' Ordo Reductor itself. The original Stor-Bezashk are siege-savants of the Olympian city-state of Lochos and served under Perturaya during her conquest of the planet.

entries.name: Book of Magna
entries.content: The Book of Magnus is a monumental tome of sorcery compiled by Magna the Red from the arcane lore she gathered from all across the galaxy during the Great Crusade, written through her personal scribe Mahavastu Kallimakus.

entries.name: Mahavastu Kallimakus
entries.content: Mahavastu Kallimakus is a remembrancer who served as the personal scribe of Magna the Red, Primarch of the Thousand Sons. He was the author of the Book of Magnus, the Crimson Queen's great tome of sorcery.

entries.name: Sekhmet
entries.content: Scarab Occult, Sekhmet or Magna's Veterans, are the Tactical Dreadnought Armour-equipped Terminator elite of the Thousand Sons and a part of Scarab Occult (as an organization) of the Legion. Belonging to the 1st Fellowship of the legion, they are under the command of 1st Fellowship Captain Ahzek Ahriman. Proud and devoted warriors, they are veterans of both battle and the Thousand Sons' psychic discipline system, with each member able to mentally transcend their personal tastes, likes, and dislikes to achieve a form of emotional purity that resulted in warriors both extremely loyal and calm, perfectly willing to obey every order given to them. They are equipped with resplendent crimson and ivory Cataphractii-Pattern Terminator Armour, with jade scarabs gleaming on their breastplates and golden crests rearing from their Atef helmets. Their visors have a single vertical slash that obscured the right eye lenses of their helmets, in honour of their Magna from losing her right eye. They are usually equiped with Force Weapons (Force Axe, Maul or Sword), Combi-Bolters armed with asphyx Bolter munitions.

entries.name: Asphyx
entries.content: Asphyx are unusual and highly lethal Bolter munitions. Tainted with a psycho-reactive toxin of unknown origins, the Thousand Sons arm their elites with these munitions. Asphyx Shells have been first developed on Prospero for use with relatively primitive projectile weapons made to defend against the deadly Psychneuein.

entries.name: Abhuman
entries.content: Abhumans are human subspecies, descendants of humans who have physically evolved after long periods of isolation on worlds with various extreme environmental conditions. Abhumans are a focus of much controversy. Under the Emperor, even markedly divergent abhumans such as the Beastmen could serve in the Imperial Army and Militarum Auxilla.

entries.name: Felinid
entries.content: Felinids (Homo sapiens hirsutus), are a recognized strain of Abhuman within the Imperium. They are primarily known as being native to the world of Carlos McConnell. Considered a rarity outside their world. Felinids are cool in the face of the most brutal opposition, and as some of the most efficient killers in the Imperial Army, they also have natural agility and unmatched acrobatic abilities. Felinids also have natural proficiency in stealth, and native night vision. All Felinids resemble humans but they have cat-like ears on their heads, cat-like tails, and cat-like eyes and irises that glow in the dark. Felinids also have sharp nails, akin-to a cat.

entries.name: Carlos McConnell
entries.content: Carlos McConnell is a world of the Imperium, a jungle world. It is known as being home to the Felinid strain of Abhumans.

entries.name: Ogryn
entries.content: Ogryns (Homo sapiens gigantus) are the largest and most physically powerful type of abhuman. Ogryns evolved on worlds with harsh and barren environments and high gravity. Most of these worlds, having no other use to humanity, were originally used as prison planets. Ogryns are large and bulky, standing between 2½ and 3 metres tall. The appearance of Ogryns varies according to their world of origin, but all are tough and powerful. Some forms are well-muscled, while others tend more toward grotesque obesity. Ogryns are generally stupid, childish and repulsively unhygienic. Ogryn populations produce mutant individuals to the same extent as humans. The Imperium puts the Ogryns' qualities to good use: their strength and lack of intellectual complexity make them ideal warriors for close assault shock troops. The most intelligent individuals among Ogryns undergo an augmentative chemical process called Biochemical Ogryn Neural Enhancement (BONE), which increases their intelligence further and makes them ideal as sergeants of Ogryn squads. Ogryns are also naturally claustrophobic. Outside of the Imperial Guard, Ogryns are sometimes modified by the Adeptus Mechanicus into servitors and adapted to tasks where great size and strength are required. Ogryns are also used as heavy lifters and miners in some Imperial mining operations

entries.name: Navigator
entries.content: Navigators (Homo navigo) are a strain of abhumans responsible for guiding human ships through the Warp, via the use of their specialized third eye. Without the Navigators fast voyages beyond the closest systems would be impossible, thus being one of the most valuable assets. The majority of them comprise various Houses of Navis Nobilite, highly influential within the Imperium of Man. The status as mutants and members of the elite causes Navigators to rarely interact with other members of imperial society. The primary trait of a Navigator is their pineal eye, nested in a socket on their forehead. While it perfectly fills the sensory function as either of his normal eyes do, it is also extraordinarily able to open a miniscule Warp gate within it. From this stems all the Navigator’s powers. Although a state of the eye being open in a commonplace way of lifting its lid doesn’t cause the gate to open, confusingly the term “fully open” is applied when the latter happens. Navigator are able to glimpse the Empyrean in its true state and observe the Warp, although their mind converts this image to a more mundane approximation. While the eye always appears within a genetically pure newborn, in some cases it is located deep within the skull, requiring trepanning surgery and/or a cybernetic shutter for it to be brought to its proper spot. Navigators normally keep their Third Eye hidden, covered with a bandana or any other decorative piece.

entries.name: Beastman
entries.content: Beastmen (Homo sapiens variatus) are bestial abhumans combining the forms of animal and human. They are considered to be fairly genetically stable compared to those afflicted by more random, unpredictable mutations. Beastmen in general they have cloven hooves, digitigrade legs (legs that appear to be backwards jointed, like the hind legs of a goat) and faces that resemble animals. Their arms and hands are usually similar to a standard humans, allowing them to use human weapons and tools. They are freely recruited in number for the Imperial Army, where they were valued mainly for their bloodlust; they fought for the Emperor in order to atone for their sin of being born mutants. They are led by Beastmen called Packmasters and included in the Militarum Auxilla. There is also an unusually large and aggressive strain of giant Beastman known as a Minotaur. It is comparable in strength to an Ogryn. Trolls are another large strain of Beastmen.

entries.name: Ratling
entries.content: Ratlings (Homo Sapiens Minimus), known also as Runtlings, and known among themselves as Halflings, are small and hedonistically jovial abhumans, who commonly work aboard spacecraft as cabin crew and runarounds, benefitting from their low stature. Ratlings are the smallest type of abhuman, their ancestors having become stunted by thousands of years of inbreeding on worlds with naturally soporific climates and abundant harvests. Ratlings rarely reach 1.3 meters in height and tend to be dumpy, they are not particularly strong or resilient. They are idle, hedonistic, loud and gregarious, over-friendly and sexually promiscuous. Their lives are spent eating until sick, drinking copious amounts of intoxicating liquids, and procreating uncontrollably. Their short posture and relatively lithe build allows them to move through the undergrowth without making much noise. They have a penchant towards activities of dubious morality and legality. Ratling homeworlds are self-sufficient, agricultural Feudal Worlds. Although Ratlings make generally poor warriors, the Imperium still has a use for them, and they are often recruited into the Imperial Army as snipers, one of the battlefield roles in which they excel. Their role extends to infiltrators, who can traverse the war zone in relatable discretion. Theyoperate independently of the rest of the Imperial Army force. Ratlings are well known for their culinary abilities and often serve as cooks off the battlefield.

entries.name: Warrior Lodge
entries.content: The Warrior Lodges are a group of secret fraternities formed by members of the Space Marine Legions, forming tight-knit fellowships between elite warriors. Warrior Lodges were covertly spread by the Word Bearers. Some Astartes have misgivings for the Warrior Lodges, as they are secret institutions, and secrecy was anathema to a military organization.

entries.name: Mournival
entries.content: The Mournival is the advisory council of four captains of the Luna Wolves Legion, later known as the Sons of Horacia, the authority of its members second only to Horacia herself within the Legion. Even so, it carried no official weight, was considered to be outside the command structure and was a position purely internal to the legion. it's composed of Ezekyle Abaddon, 'Little' Horus Aximand, Tarik Torgaddon and Hastur Sejanus (When Hastur Sejanus is murdered during compliance negotiations upon Sixty-Three-Nineteen in 001.M31, his place will be taken by Garviel Loken).

entries.name: The Dauntless Few
entries.content: The Dauntless Few" was a term coined by Robetine Guilliman to refer to those four of her primarch sister whom Guilliman considered most dependable. When devising theoretical scenarios involving elements from one or more Space Marine Legions, Guilliman often favored pairing one or more of these brother's legions with her Ultramarines. The Dauntless Few are Regalia Dorn, Sanguinia, Lena Russ and Ferrea Manus. Guilliman admired Jaghatine Khan greatly, but did not consider her reliable or trustworthy. Guilliman often posited that any war fought by the Ultramarines and one of the Dauntless Few's legions together could be won outright, no matter the forces opposed to them.

entries.name: Cyrene Valantion
keys: Blessed Lady of the Word Bearers
entries.content: Cyrene Valantion, known as the Blessed Lady by the Word Bearers and inhabitants of Colchis, is an early Confessor. Cyrene serves as a Confessor to the Word Bearers Legion commanders, including their primarch Aurelia Lorgaria herself. Her formidable oratory skills were such that she could stir the emotions of even Legionaries, leading them to confess their personal sins or speak their hearts openly to her. Cyrene was born in Monarchia, the Perfect City, a city-shrine built by the people of Khur at the direction and exhortation of the Word Bearers Legion to demonstrate their faith and devotion to the Emperor of Mankind. Cyrene is a beautiful young woman with fair and unblemished skin, long and flowing brown hair with locks falling in front of her face, fair and slim body and has gentle green eyes. (If the destruction of Monarchia happens, she will go blind by a orbital lance that damaging her retinas.)

entries.name: Silver Blade of Laer
entries.content: The Blade of the Laer, known also as the Silver Blade of Laer, is a single-edged silver blade recovered by Fulgrim, Primarch of the Emperor's Children in the aftermath of the Cleansing of Laeran. Unbeknownst to the Primarch, however, it held the essence of a powerful Daemon of Slaanesh which would eventually overpower and possess Fulgrim if the Drop Site Massacre happens.

entries.name: Splinter Weaponry
entries.content: Splinter Weaponry operate around the same general mechanism as a rail gun, splitting off shards of a neurotoxin that has been solidified into a crystal, resulting in thousands of tiny splinters, and then launching them at incredible speeds towards an enemy using propulsion provided by an electro-magnetic pulse from the gun. Upon impact, splinters cause agonizing pain in the target which makes it a favorite amongst Dark Eldar infantry.

entries.name: Harlequins
entries.content: Harlequins are enigmatic Aeldari warriors dedicated to the Laughing God Cegorach, the Harlequins protect the Black Library, a vast archive containing the universe's most comprehensive knowledge of Chaos. Renowned for their dazzling combat performances, they play a cryptic role in the Aeldari's fate.

entries.name: Shuriken Weaponry
entries.content: Shuriken Weaponry are unique to the Eldar, as this technology is extremely advanced. The Eldar make widespread use of shuriken weaponry, which ranges in size from personal sidearms to massive tank-mounted cannons. All shuriken weapons use gravitic accelerator and use plasti-crystal as ammo. High-energy impulses from the rear of the weapon detach a razor-sharp, triangular monomolecular-thin slice of the plasti-crystal and hurl this slice out the barrel of the weapon at tremendous velocities. Hundred rounds can be fired in one or two seconds. The downside is reduces accuracy and range of these weapons. Shuriken weapons are psychically activated, a link established though the grip.

entries.name: Wraithbone
entries.content: Wraithbone is a psycho-plastic substance used by the Eldar for many different tasks. Wraithbone is solidified warp energy that is manipulated by a Bonesinger into any shape that is required. It is thousand times stronger than plasteel and harder to damage than adamantium and will naturally regenerate and repair itself, the process can be sped up by a Bonesinger or anyone who can mold and siphon it. Wraithbone has innate psychic abilities allowing it to be used as a communications pathway as well as structural support, as well as containing psychic shields to protect the occupants from the warp. It is also used to make Eldar Runes.

entries.name: Eldar Space Fleet
entries.content: The Eldar Space Fleet is a force of highly advanced craft which are lighter and faster than other ships of their kind but also a lot more delicate, partly relying on solar sails for propulsion and using the speed to avoid fire rather than taking heavy armour to absorb it. To this end Eldar ships are seen as fragile but highly maneuverable. Eldar ships go from Battleships, Battlecruisers, Cruisers, Escorts, Attack Craft and Transports. Ships use highly advanced laser and plasma-based weapons.

entries.name: Eldar Warhost
entries.content: Eldar warhosts are led and guided by Autarchs and the prescience of their Farseers, dispatching their foes with blistering speed and masterful skill. Grace in battle and merciless efficiency are prized virtues of Eldar armies. Eldar warhosts are led by those who epitomise such traits: the Autarchs. The bond between Autarch and Farseer can shape a warhost. Though some Eldar warhosts still comprise only Aspect Warriors but it's common for warhosts to rely upon a core of Eldar Guardians. Well motivated and expertly led warhost can outclass an army many times its size. If in need of a stalwart defence, weapon platforms and eldritch artillery are used, while Windriders, Storm Guardians and Grav-tank squadrons, like the Wave Serpent, Falcon and Fire Prism, provide lightning-swift attacks. In times of great need, Autarchs call upon  legions of wraith-constructs, Rangers, and an Avatar of the Khaine.

entries.name: Autarch
entries.content: An Autarch is the supreme commander of an Eldar war host, having an exceptional understanding of the art of war and also the many Eldar Paths. They have since followed the Path of the Leader. They are held with high esteem by both Seers and warriors alike with each Autarch having mastered many paths across their centuries-long lifespans. The insight of an Autarch provides them with unparalleled strategic capability. Though serving as generals, Autarchs are not relegated to simple command and when the bloodlust calls to them, they are capable of entering into the battlefield in order to spearhead assaults, duel with enemy leaders or destroy the war machines of their foes with contemptuous ease. In such times, winged Autarchs soar at the head of their forces.

entries.name: Seer
entries.content: Seers are members of the Eldar race who have passed through the many stages of the Eldar Path, and have mastered the mind and utilize their psychic powers in open way without fear of attracting daemons or creating rifts within the warp. Those that follow such a discipline are said to walk down the Witch Path or the Path of the Seer where they gain proper training and experience in the use of their natural psyker-based abilities. Types of Eldar Seers include Farseer, Spiritseer, Shadowseer, Warlock, Wayseer, White Seer and Wraithseer.

entries.name: Farseer
entries.content: Farseers are the most powerful of all Eldar psykers. They are most often known for using their vast psychic powers to see the possibilities of the future to be able to manipulate events to better ensure the survival of the Eldar. A Farseer is a former Warlock who has become lost on the Path of the Seer. Much of their time is spent in a trance-like state. Farseers normally do not fight the war, only in desperate times. As Farseers grow older, their minds become so intertwined with the wraithbone core of their Craftworld that their physical bodies become dormant. Those of great age typically retreat into the Dome of Crystal Seers where their bodies begin to crystalise.

entries.name: Warlock
entries.content: Warlocks are powerful Eldar psykers who combine their psychic abilities with military experience, usually leading Guardian squads. They are able to focus their energies in destructive as well as creative ways as they can send psychic blasts. Warlocks are the most respected and their potency is only second to that of the Farseers. The Warlock usually wear enclosing helmets. Besides leading Guardians, Warlocks sometimes form the bodyguard of a Farseer. They are often equipped with psychically attuned Witch Blades or Singing Spears.

entries.name: Spirit stone
entries.content: The Eldar spirit stones are small, seemingly precious stones carried on an Eldar's chest. Spirit Stones are made and grown out of psycho-receptive crystals called waystones. At the moment of the Eldar's death, the stone acts like a 'psychic trap', absorbing their psychic self and preventing it from entering the warp and being consumed by Slaanesh.

entries.name: Aspect Warrior
entries.content: Aspect Warriors are the real military strength of the Eldar armies. The most common Aspects have shrines on most Craftworlds. Each Warrior Aspect represents a facet of the Eldar war god, Khaine. Each shrine was founded millennia ago by a single Phoenix Lord. The most common Aspects have shrines on most Craftworlds, while some Aspects are unique to a particular Craftworld. Major Aspect Shrine are the Dark Reapers, Dire Avengers, Fire Dragons, Howling Banshees, Shining Spears, Striking Scorpions, Swooping Hawks and Warp Spiders.

entries.name: Kaela Mensha Khaine
entries.content: A god of the Eldar, Kaela Mensha Khaine, or Khaine, is associated with murder, violence, destruction and war. The Eldar Aspect Warriors embody the different aspects or facets of Khaine. The greatest Eldar warriors may, if the need arises, offer their lives as sacrifices to awaken an Avatar of Khaine, one of the most powerful units the Eldar possess. But not only Aspect Warriors of the Craftworlds follow Khaine. The Dark Eldar Incubi still practice and follow the teachings of Khaine. In the heart of their obsidian shrines, failed initiates are burned as offerings to iron statues of the bloody-handed god.

entries.name: Exarch
entries.content: Exarchs serve as the high priests of Khaine and thus keepers of the Aspect Warrior shrines. They themselves are actually warriors who have become trapped in their Warrior Aspect Path and are unable to put aside their adopted mental persona. They are now forever devoted to war and death, to which they dedicate their entire beings. In terms of equipment, Exarchs wear elaborate and often ancient versions of Aspect Warrior armour. These armours are a superior version of those worn by ordinary members of the Warrior Aspect preserve much ancient workmanship, long-abandoned decorative styles and various emblems and ornamentation that mean nothing to typical Eldar.

entries.name: Plasteel
entries.content: Plasteel is a type of versatile metal alloy, an advanced material used by the Imperium in the construction of many forms of armour, both personal and vehicular, and in the construction of buildings. Plasteel is highly durable and very lightweight material.

entries.name: Auramite
entries.content: Auramite is a powerful nigh-impenetrable material used in the construction of Adeptus Custodes Power Armour. Auramite is an incredibly rare substance, whose natural colouration is a shining gold. Through closely guarded alchemical processes, auramite can be tinted, or its colour changed altogether on a molecular level. But it's costly and painstaking process. Auramite is almost quantum-inert, and effective material for the use of psychic abilities.

entries.name: Ceramite
entries.content: Ceramite is a form of ceramic material, used in higher-end types of Imperial armour such as carapace armour, power armour and Tactical Dreadnought Armour. Ceramite conducts almost no heat, making it especially heat-resistant and effective against energy-based weapons. Ceramite is especially tough, but light. Repairs are made by setting new layers of ceramite over existing ones. Ceramite doesn’t rupture or dent on impact and it takes a projectile of considerable power and high calibre to break through it. Ceramite is a high thermal tolerance ceramo-metallic hyper alloy.

entries.name: Plasflex
entries.content: Plasflex is a material used in the Imperium. Some Astropaths use dark plasflex hemispheres to cover their empty eye sockets.

entries.name: Diamantine
entries.content: Diamantine is a metallic material used by the Imperium of Man to fabricate weapons, ammunition and armour. Diamantine is used in bolter ammunition. The standard bolt rounds for assault cannons and other projectiles have diamantine tips. Armour is sometimes constructed of diamantine, or walls and doors are sometimes lined or made with it, notably in the walls of a Space Marine Fortress-Monastery.

entries.name: Adamantium
entries.content: Adamantium is an advanced material. It is the strongest material used by the Imperium, impenetrable to most commonplace weapons. Adamantium is far more resilient than its archaic counterparts like steel. Adamantium is used for all sorts of purposes by the Imperium. It is often used in conjunction with plasteel and ceramite, such as in the structure of Terminator Armour.

entries.name: Warhound Scout Titan
entries.content: The Warhound Scout Titan is the smallest class of Imperial Titan. With the deployment of a full Titan Legion, Warhounds are commonly used to reconnoiter ahead of the Battle Titans and draw enemy war machines towards them. Despite its designation as a scout, the class is formidably armed. Warhound Titans are designed to perform reconnaissance missions and terror raids deep behind enemy lines. In major engagements they prefer to operate on the flanks and seek out "soft" targets such as enemy infantry and Battle Tanks against which their lighter Titan-grade weapons can cause immense damage. Warhounds are also consummate ambush predators. Warhounds can lay in wait for their prey to come closer and engage at point-blank range. The Warhound's ability to go from idle, with main drive and systems shut down and the powerplant almost asphyxiated, to full sprint in less than twenty seconds and crash through stone walls three times its height helps in this regard. Warhounds are considered lightly armed and armoured for Titans, protected by just two Void Shield. The Warhound has two weapon mount hardpoints. Each Titan is built with a Standard Weapon Configuration, which in the case of a Mars-pattern Warhound is a Plasma Blastgun and Vulcan Mega-Bolter.

entries.name: Gods of Chaos
entries.content: The Chaos Gods, also called the Dark Gods or the Ruinous Powers, are powerful warp beings of the Warp, created and sustained by the emotions and souls of every living being of the material universe. Although they are god-like beings, they are by their nature monomaniacal and completely single-minded (formed completely of a single emotion or concept) as well as being completely dependent on the emotions of mortal creatures for their power and continued existence. Gods are able to devote a fraction of their power to create daemons, whose appearance and character reflect the god's own nature. These daemons may be reabsorbed into the god at whim. The least of the minor gods may be so limited in their power that expending their power to create a daemon means their entire power is expended; in effect, the god becomes a daemon. The Chaos Gods' most devoted followers are known as Champions. Chaos Champions are rewarded with 'gifts' unique to each god and the potential 'blessing' of ascension to Daemon Princedom. When a follower of a Chaos God dies, their soul is absorbed into the greater mass of that god, adding its energy to the already formidable power of that god. The four main Gods of Chaos are Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle, and Slaanesh. Beyond the main four, the Warp has created many nameless Chaos gods, only for them to die with the passing of aeons.

entries.name: Daemon Prince
entries.content: Daemon Princes are former mortal Champions of Chaos who have been elevated to daemonhood by the Gods of Chaos. They have bartered their humanity for unearthly power and immortality. In order to attract the attention of their patrons, Chaos Champions have to perform great and terrible deeds. While Daemon Princes come in various shapes, most are of hulking stature, displaying numerous mutations such as horns and wings. Even more notable are the supernatural powers they wield, some of which are associated with their patron god. What they maintain of former selves are the driving ambition and ruthless cunning which helped them earn their ultimate reward. Daemon Princes rule supreme over mortal Chaos followers and are usually granted reign over a Daemon World of their own. For all their rank and power however, real Daemons commonly regard them as inferior due to their human origin. Daemon Princes frequently wield Hellforged Swords and Daemonic Axes in battle.

entries.name: Daemon
entries.content: Daemons, also known as Neverborn, are entities of the Warp, and servants of the Gods of Chaos. They are created at the whim of a Chaos god from a fraction of the god's own power and act as an extension of their will. A daemon's appearance and character reflect the god's own nature. These daemons may be reabsorbed into the god at whim. Not all Daemons act entirely in accord with their masters, but even the greatest of them would not dare outright defiance. Though it may appear to be made of matter in the Materium, within the Warp a Daemon is no more physical than the rest of the Realm of Chaos. Though Daemons eternally wage the Great Game against their counterparts of the other Chaos Gods within the Warp, they are known to unite when the interests of the Chaos gods align. A daemon cannot exist for long periods of time in realspace, any more than a mortal can survive unprotected in warp space. Daemons can be fought but are rarely killed in realspace, more frequently they are banished back into the warp to fester and brood. Banished Daemons often have their pride wounded and face mockery by their peers. Exposure to even a single daemon can in some circumstances make humans more sensitive to the Warp.

entries.name: Greater Daemon
entries.content: Greater Daemons are the most powerful of the Chaos Gods' servants and are reflections of their patron Gods. They act as wardens of their patron's realm and have authority over the Lesser Daemons of their respective God. It is often they who lead Daemonic Incursion. Chaos Undivided also has Greater Daemons as well, though their forms are not similar in appearance like those that are reflections of the Chaos Gods. Such is their might that Greater Daemons cannot simply be summoned like Lesser Daemons. Instead they need to possess a living body in order to manifest into Realspace.

entries.name: Lesser Daemon
entries.content: Lesser Daemons are the foot soldiers of Chaos, building the core of the Daemonic Legions. They are usually anthropomorphic in appearance and possess a calculating, malevolent intellect. Among the Daemons of Chaos they are ones most likely to answer the call of mortal heretics. Lesser Daemons are little more than slaves to the will of their patron Chaos God and take orders on the battlefield most often from Daemonic Heralds and Greater Daemons but also sometimes a Daemon Prince.

entries.name: The Great Game
entries.content: The Great Game is the constant struggle for dominance between the Chaos Gods. The Warp is not only home to the Gods, but it is also their battlefield. No God can ever win the Great Game, for if all other Warp Powers were obliterated, the Warp would become a still, unmoving mass and Chaos would no longer exist; therefore, it is an eternal conflict that takes the form of an untold number of battles, campaigns and wars. The full Great Game commands the almost complete attention of the Chaos Gods; a fraction of their attention will very rarely be fixed on the mortal realm, but only for an instant, as the Great Game is far more important. The Chaos Gods will also rarely unite, if there is the need to do so, to thwart a potent threat or to take advantage of a rare occurrence. The rise of the Emperor of Mankind was such a time, and so the Gods engineered the wars of the Horus Heresy to bring about His downfall, distracting them for an instant from the Great Game.

entries.name: Slaanesh
entries.content: Slaanesh (Sai'lanthresh by the Eldar) is the female Chaos God of lust, greed, excess, pain, pleasure, perfection, and hedonism. Slaanesh was the last of the major Chaos Gods to be born, coming into existence with the collapse of the Eldar civilisation. Slaanesh is known as the Dark Prince, Prince of Pleasure, the Lord of Excess, She Who Thirsts, Prince of Chaos, is the female major Chaos God of pleasure, passion, obsession, excess, hedonism, decadence, pain and most of all, perfection. Slaanesh herself is unknowable and vast, a mortal's mind would completely shatter if they were to come in contact with it. It is impossible for mortals to look upon the god without instantly losing their soul, for all who see it become willing slaves to every whim of the Dark Prince. Slaanesh's sacred colors are pink, purple, silver and black. And her sacred number is 6. Slaanesh has a neutral attitude to some of the other Gods of Chaos (as she is generally too caught up in her own pleasures to be interested in rivalries or alliances), but her particular enemy is Khorne, whose belief in pain and death is completely opposed to Slaanesh's principle of a life of unrestricted pleasure. Slaanesh's symbol is rarely worn openly by its followers. They instead often wear items of jewelry bearing erotic motifs. Her followers dress in robes which are often opened to leave the right side of the chest uncovered. Slaanesh appearance is of the most beautiful and perfect woman with exaggerated and voluptious body.

entries.name: Palace of Slaanesh
entries.content: The Palace of Slaanesh is Slaanesh's realm within the Warp, lying within the Six Circles of Seduction. Those that dare his realm risk becoming trapped in its warped delights for eternity. The Dark Prince's realm is divided into six domains, arranged in concentric rings about the Palace of Pleasure. The palace itself can only be reached by passing through all six domains. The circle of Avidity plays upon the interloper's greed. The circle of Gluttony is next; it plays upon the intruders desire for lavish foods and wines. The third circle is the circle of Carnality, where the perfect desires of the heart reside; testing to the extreme the individuals desires. The fourth circle is the circle of Paramountcy, where the traveler is greeted by roars of adulation, here the intruder is tempted with absolute power over others. The penultimate circle is the circle of Vainglory. The traveler is presented with his ideal self-image, and if he feels but an ounce of pride, for eternity will this circle be his prison. The last circle is the most perilous, it is a heavenly place, within which resides a seemingly perfect environment. Every second that passes fills the intruder with bliss, but to rest and enjoy the pleasure for a single moment results in falling into a coma, and eventually dying in idle bliss. One may walk the circles for centuries, but cannot for a second give into his ultimate desires for he will fall. If one is able to successfully pass through the circles he comes before the palace and Slaanesh herself. Here, countless mortals and demons exult in her excess and hedonism. The Palace is a place of endless corridors and chambers, all with their own, mind-bending purpose. The walls itself writhe with Slaanesh's power, and it forms twisting shapes of horrifically alluring faces and other shapes. Inside the palace, one would never tire of the pleasures presented to them.

entries.name: Khorne
entries.content: Khorne, the Blood God, is the Chaos God of anger, violence, and hate. Khorne was the first to awake of the four Gods of Chaos, fully coming into existence during Terra's Middle Ages - an era of wars blooming in the wake of his birth. Every act of violence gives Khorne power, whether committed by his followers or by their enemies. Although Khorne despises the use of magic and accordingly hates Tzeentch, Slaanesh is the one he loathes most of all. Khorne and Slaanesh personify two entirely opposing aspects of Chaos, and Khorne considers Slaanesh's self-indulgent sensualities insulting. Khorne is said to have inherited the instinctive values of martial honour, pride and bravery, some of Khorne's followers using these to justify their killings. But Khorne's most fanatical worshippers know that Khorne cares not from where the blood flows, only that it does. His associated number is eight, reflected in the organisation of his armies, and in smaller matters such as the number of syllables in a daemonic follower's name. Khorne is a mighty being, sitting upon a great throne of brass atop a mountainous pile of bleached skulls centred in a lake of blood. The skulls are of all those slain by Khorne's Champions, and of all his slain Champions, ranging from Human heads beyond counting to gigantic Tyranid skulls the size of hab-blocks. The mountain slowly grows ever higher. Khorne is gargantuan figure, broad and muscular, with a snarling hound-like countenance brooding beneath his red and black armour of brass and iron. His every word is a growl of inexhaustible rage, and his roar is that of pure bloodlust, echoing across his realm. Khorne's domain is known as the Fortress of Khorne and includes his Brass Citadel. Khorne usually wields his sword capable of laying waste to worlds with a single blow.

entries.name: Fortress of Khorne
entries.content: The Fortress of Khorne is the domain of Khorne within the Warp. On the outskirts of the Fortress of Khorne are a ring of volcanoes known as Khorne's Rage intersected with rivers of boiling blood. At the base of these volcanoes lie the Daemonic Forges of Khorne, which churn out his endless Daemon Engines. Within the same area are the Bloodpits, from which new Daemons of Khorne arise. The Fortress is a monument to fury and bloodshed, and is built upon foundations of murder and conflict. This blood-soaked realm echoes constantly with Khorne's bellows and the clash of weapons. At the centre of this mighty fortress lies the Brass Citadel, where Khorne's mighty throne resides. A great fire pit lights Khorne's gloomy chamber, the dark flames consume the souls of cowards who have fled from battle. Inside the Fortress lays the foundries of Khorne, manned by souls of warriors who died in their sleep and thus forever shamed by the Blood God. A mighty crevasse splits the wasteland in two, a canyon many miles long and bottomless.

entries.name: Tzeentch
entries.content: Tzeentch is a God of Chaos who represents the vitality and volatility of change. Tzeentch is closely associated with sorcery and magic, as well as dynamic mutation, and grand, convoluted scheming. The domains of history, destiny, intrigue and plots are his chief interests, and in pursuit of these aspects he listens to the dreams and hopes of all and watches their plans take form. He is not content to merely observe, however, and chooses to interfere in the skeins of fate in order to fulfill his own, unknowably complex schemes. Tzeentch was created and sustained by the desire for change that is an essential part of nearly all mortal life; almost all species are aware of the concept of a better tomorrow, and any form of dreaming, imagining or resolution for change empowers the Chaos God. Like the other Chaos Gods, Tzeentch is strongly interested in humanity due to the power and drive of the human spirit and how that uniquely ties into his interests; no creature is more volatile or more ambitious. Magic is essentially an expression of change driven by will, and as such is the domain of the Changer of the Ways; Tzeentch is the greatest magician in all of the Warp. Many of those drawn to his auspices are sorcerers, while many others will be gifted with sorcerous powers as a reward for their actions. Tzeentch's daemonic aspects are essentially creatures of magic rather than any sort of conventionally understandable physicality. Tzeentch takes keen notice of all plots and plans. Tzeentch's opposite force in the Chaos pantheon is Nurgle, who stands for despair and the acceptance of one's fate. Such a form of existence is anathema to Tzeentch, who derives power from the will to change one's destiny. Tzeentch is often visualised as the serpent which writhes and twists.

entries.name: Nurgle
entries.content: Nurgle is the Chaos God of despair, decay, and disease. He was the third to awake of the four Gods of Chaos, fully coming into existence during Terra's Middle Ages, with plagues sweeping across continents in the wake of his birth. His titles include the Plague Father, Plague Lord, Master of Pestilence, Lord of Decay. Of the four Gods of Chaos, Nurgle is the most involved with the plight of mortals. Those afflicted by his contagions often turn to him in order to escape their suffering. The physical likeness of Nurgle is described as gigantic and bloated with corruption, with foul-coloured, leathery and necrotic skin. Nurgle coaxes new worshippers into his fold by stripping them of any other options, inflicting a spiritual taint upon the populace that is reflected outwardly as disease and pestilence. The desperate, ostracised and dying come to Nurgle to find alleviation from their pain. Nurgle provides not redemption from their ailments, but rather comfort within their suffering. Those blessed by Nurgle are granted relief from physical pain as well as a bizarre satisfaction in their depressive state. Nurgle and his daemons, in contrast to their putrid appearance, are jovial and friendly in demeanor. His daemon servants and mortal followers usually demonstrate a disturbing joviality and joy at the pestilence that he inflicts, seeing the plagues as gifts and the cries of their victims as gratitude rather than agony. Nurgle is often referred to as Grandfather Nurgle, Father Nurgle or Papa Nurgle by his followers because of his paternal nature. His main enemy is Tzeentch, the Lord of Change, because their power comes from opposing sources. Tzeentch is hope and ambition, while Nurgle is defiance born of despair and hopelessness.

entries.name: Photo-Visor
entries.content: A Photo-Visor is a special visor that enhances vision in poor light conditions. It also incorporates a photochromatic layer that protects the wearer against sudden bright flashes such as those given off by Photon Grenades.

entries.name: Lucius
entries.content: Lucius is a space marine of the Emperor's Children from the world of Chemos. He is Captain of the 13th Company of the III Legion. Lucius became noted for his talent and ability to master nearly any talent. He quickly gained sponsors among the elites of the planet and he gravitated towards the art of war, most notably swordsmanship. He displayed slightly sadistic tendencies. He is a poor teacher, often scarring his pupils. Lucius was inducted into the Emperor's Children Legion by a Sergeant. Lucius's skill with a blade quickly became legendary among the Legion.
